research.method: Dedicated research subagent; statute text retrieved from lawphil.net. Every row carries the specific provision, a source URL, a confidence and a review status.
research.warning: review_status=verified means the provision was retrieved and checked. It is not legal advice, and pending rows still need a human legal reviewer.

new_laws.title: An Act to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing, Amending RA 8550 (Philippine Fisheries Code)
new_laws.summary: Covers damage to coral reefs (Section 96), destructive fishing gear and methods (Section 97), and conversion of mangroves (Section 99). Replaced RA 8550 Chapter VI, so the RA 8550 sections 91-92 are no longer the operative text.

law_title_updates.title: National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act, as amended by RA 11038
law_title_updates.reason: RA 11038 replaced the prohibited-acts and penalty sections. A row citing only the 1992 text points at superseded law.

links.rationale: The Clean Air Act is the only listed statute that sets air-emission limits and penalises exceedance.
links.note: §20 bans incineration of municipal/biomedical/hazardous waste but exempts siga and traditional/agricultural burning; §47 is the residual penalty clause.

links.rationale: §96 makes it unlawful to commit any activity that damages coral reefs; §97 bans muro-ami and other gear or methods destructive to coral.
links.note: No in-list statute covers coral damage generally. RA 7586 §20(e) (as amended by RA 11038) applies only inside NIPAS areas; RA 9275 §27(a) only where a discharge caused the damage.

links.rationale: RA 6969 is the dedicated hazardous-waste statute: §13(d) prohibits keeping hazardous waste in storage anywhere in the Philippines, and §15 authorises administrative fines.
links.note: The IRR supplies handling/transport/disposal standards; §14(b) is the criminal penalty for §13(d). If the waste reaches water, RA 9275 §27(f)-(g); household hazardous special wastes also touch RA 9003 §3(pp).

links.rationale: §68 is the illegal-logging provision: cutting, gathering or removing timber or forest products from forest land without a licence, with confiscation of timber and equipment.
links.note: RA 7161 inserted the NIRC forest-charge sections as PD 705 §§68-77 and renumbered the old §§68-68-B, so confirm the number in a consolidated code. RA 11038 §20(c) applies inside protected areas; RA 9175 covers chainsaw possession/use.

links.rationale: §48(3) expressly prohibits the open burning of solid waste and §49(b) supplies the penalty; §3(kk) includes agricultural waste within solid waste.
links.note: RA 8749 §20 bans incineration of municipal/biomedical/hazardous waste but expressly exempts traditional small-scale siga and agricultural/cultural/health/food-preparation burning, so it is not the general hook. RA 9003 penalties are low (₱300-₱1,000), so LGUs often add ordinances.

links.rationale: RA 11038 replaced the 1992 squatting clause with §20(n), which prohibits occupying or dwelling on public land inside a protected area without PAMB clearance; §21(b) sets the penalty.
links.note: Cite the RA 11038 text, not the 1992 original. Fine is now ₱200,000-₱1,000,000 and/or 1-6 years. §§20(a)-(e) cover poaching, wildlife collection, timber cutting and destructive gear inside protected areas.

links.rationale: §48(1) prohibits littering, throwing or dumping waste in public places including roads, canals, esteros and parks, which is the exact conduct in a citizen dumping report.
links.note: Open dumping in flood-prone areas: §48(6). Operating an open dump: §48(9) (₱500,000 plus 5-10% of net annual income). LGU ordinances may carry higher fines.

links.rationale: §27(a) prohibits discharging material into a water body that causes pollution, and §27(i) prohibits discharging regulated pollutants without a valid permit; §28 fines ₱10,000-₱200,000 per day.
links.note: PD 1067 Art. 75/91(B)(5) is narrower (water-supply sources only); PD 979 §3(a) excludes industrial/manufacturing effluents, so it cannot anchor this code.

links.rationale: §27(e) makes trading of wildlife unlawful and §28 scales the penalty by the species' threat category; §5(t) defines trade to include purchase, sale, export and import.
links.note: §27(f) collecting/possessing and §27(i) transporting are usually charged with (e). Inside protected areas RA 11038 §20(a)-(b) applies; RA 10654 §102 covers aquatic CITES species.

links.rationale: §99 is the most specific national provision for mangrove conversion.
links.note: PD 705 reaches only mangrove classified as forest land. For Palawan, PCSD rules under RA 7611 §19(8) apply in addition.

links.rationale: §43 bars clear-cutting of mangrove swamps set aside for coast protection and §69 penalises destruction of forest land; §3(o) defines mangrove as a forest type.
links.note: Fallback only: PD 705 applies where the mangrove is classified as forest land. Kept as a secondary link for that case.

links.rationale: §4(a) prohibits discharging oil, noxious or other harmful substances from vessels or man-made structures at sea into Philippine waters, and §7 provides the penalty.
links.note: Confirmed for vessel/platform spills. §3(a) excludes industrial/manufacturing effluents, so land-based discharges fall under RA 9275 §27; §4(b) covers shore-based dumping of refuse; RA 9483 governs compensation.

remove_links.reason: Rejected by review: RA 7611 is Palawan-only and even there is a framework statute, not the offence-creating law. It has no penal section; penalties come only from PCSD rules under §19(8).
